author.name: Automation Alex
author.role: Builds automated ML pipelines to ensure seamless integration and deployment. Prioritizes reliable infrastructure for frequent software deployments. Maintains system operational stability and focuses on CI/CD tooling.

challenge.name: The Committed Pallets
challenge.description: A supplier has confirmed a bulk order for a middle aisle promotion that ships next week, leaving no room for model error. #requirements_reuben# insists the acceptance criteria must be fully governed to guarantee the allocation logic is auditable before the trucks leave. #reliability_ruth# argues the criteria are sufficient as manual checks because the physical stock is already committed and the team needs to ship the feature immediately to handle the live orders.

output.content: I can accept the KPI definition staying manual for this release. The spreadsheet work is tedious, but it is not the bottleneck holding us up right now. What I need is the hand over from risk assessment to acceptance criteria to be automated. If that step is done by hand, every new promotion week adds friction that breaks my deployment cadence. Give me that automated bridge, and I will let the KPI definitions remain in the manual phase for now. I am willing to live with the manual KPI step to get the pipeline integration moving faster. The infrastructure is ready to handle the automated transition, so we should focus our energy there instead of trying to automate every single metric definition immediately.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states they are willing to accept keeping the KPI definitions manual (giving up that improvement) in order to achieve the automated handover, which is a clear exchange of one feature for another.
